How many sales the salesperson needs this month
The warranty cost to the likely cost of repairs
questions.explanation: A warranty is worth it only if the expected repair cost is higher than the price.

questions.question: Moral hazard refers to...
options: Changing behavior because you are protected from risk
A code of rules that insurers must follow by law
Fraud committed by banks against their customers
questions.explanation: People may take more risks when they know they are covered.

questions.question: Which behavior reduces financial risk?
questions.explanation: An emergency fund protects you from sudden costs.

questions.question: Disability insurance replaces...
options: All of your car repair costs after any accident
Your savings if the bank loses your money
Part of your income if illness or injury prevents you from working
questions.explanation: It helps cover living costs when you cannot work for a while.

questions.question: Which is a common red flag for a scam?
options: A written contract that explains all fees
A clear refund policy posted on the website
Pressure to pay right away by gift card
questions.explanation: Scammers often push fast payments that cannot be reversed.

questions.question: The risk-return tradeoff says...
options: Higher expected returns generally come with higher risk
Lower returns always come with more risk
questions.explanation: Investments that promise more growth usually carry more risk.

questions.question: Which best describes opportunity cost?
options: The price tag printed on the item you choose
The extra amount a store adds to the price to make a profit
The value of the next best alternative you give up
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of what you give up when you choose.

questions.question: Why is 100 dollars today worth more than 100 dollars in 5 years?
options: It can earn interest and inflation erodes future money
Money loses value only when you spend it at a store
Prices usually fall over time, so future money buys more
questions.explanation: Money today can grow, and inflation lowers the buying power of future money.

questions.question: A business earns 2 dollars profit per item. How many items must it sell to cover a 100-dollar startup cost?
questions.explanation: 100 divided by 2 equals 50 items.

questions.question: SMART goals are...
options: Simple, money-based, approved, reasonable, and temporary
Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound
Only long-term goals that take more than ten years
questions.explanation: SMART goals are clear enough to track and reach.

questions.question: Which is an example of a sunk cost?
options: Money you plan to spend next month on bills
Future savings you expect to earn from a job
Money already spent that cannot be recovered
questions.explanation: Sunk costs are gone, so they should not drive future choices.

questions.question: Continuing a bad purchase only because you already spent money on it is an example of...
questions.explanation: The sunk cost fallacy keeps people spending based on money already gone.

questions.question: If an extra hour of studying gives less benefit than it costs you in time, the smart move is...
options: Keep going no matter what it costs you
questions.explanation: Marginal thinking compares the next unit of effort to its benefit.

questions.question: Which step comes first when creating a budget?
questions.explanation: You need to know what comes in and goes out before planning.

questions.question: Why learn about money early?
options: Money only matters once you are an adult
Good habits compound over a lifetime
questions.explanation: Early habits build up over many years.

questions.question: Unit pricing helps you compare...
options: Which brand logo looks the best
Which store is closest to you
Cost per ounce or per item
questions.explanation: Unit price shows the real cost per unit, so you can compare sizes.

questions.question: Expected value helps you compare choices by...
options: Looking only at which choice has the lowest price
Picking whichever choice your friends picked
questions.explanation: Expected value combines the chance of each result with its payoff.

questions.question: Which is the best first financial step for a beginner?
questions.explanation: An emergency fund protects you from setbacks before you take bigger risks.

questions.question: Scarcity means...
options: Money is unlimited, so everyone can have everything
Prices never change, so planning is not needed
Resources are limited relative to wants
questions.explanation: Scarcity is why every choice involves a trade-off.

questions.question: A trade-off means...
options: Giving up one benefit to get another
Getting both choices for free with no cost
Having no costs because you chose carefully
questions.explanation: Choosing one option means giving up another.

questions.question: How often should you review your budget?
options: Only when you run out of money
questions.explanation: Regular reviews keep your budget matched to real spending.
